title: Power Outage Indicator
shortDescription: The freezer experienced a power outage that may have affected food safety.
fullDescription:
The PO code on a Maytag freezer indicates a power outage has occurred. The freezer tracks the internal temperature rise during the outage and alerts you if food safety may be compromised.

This is a notification, not a fault. Press any button to dismiss the alert after verifying food quality. If the freezer interior rose above 40F for more than 2 hours, discard perishable food.

fixSteps.title: Acknowledge the alert
fixSteps.instruction: Press any button on the control panel to silence the tone and clear the display.

fixSteps.title: Verify food safety
fixSteps.instruction: Check that food is still firm and below 40F. Discard anything that has thawed.

fixSteps.title: Check breaker
fixSteps.instruction: Verify the circuit breaker is on and the outlet is working.

whenToCallPro: No technician needed; this is an informational alert only.
videoSearchQuery: Maytag freezer PO power outage code reset

faq.a: If the freezer stayed below 40F, yes. Otherwise discard perishables.
Press any button on the control panel.

title: Freezer Temperature Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The freezer temperature sensor (thermistor) is reporting invalid readings.
fullDescription:
Error code E1 indicates the freezer compartment thermistor is open, shorted, or out of range. The control board cannot regulate cooling without a valid temperature reading.

The freezer may run constantly or not at all. Replacing the thermistor usually resolves this fault.

fixSteps.title: Unplug freezer
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect power for safety before servicing.

fixSteps.title: Test thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance; at 32F it should read approximately 16.6k ohms.

fixSteps.title: Replace thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new thermistor and reconnect wiring.

whenToCallPro: If the error persists after replacing the thermistor, the control board may be failing.

faq.q: Can I keep using the freezer?
faq.a: Not safely; temperatures cannot be regulated.

title: Evaporator Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The evaporator coil sensor is faulty or disconnected.
fullDescription:
E2 indicates the evaporator thermistor, which monitors coil temperature for defrost timing, has failed. Without this sensor, the defrost cycle may not run correctly, leading to frost buildup.

Inspect wiring at the evaporator and replace the sensor if readings are out of spec.

fixSteps.title: Remove rear freezer panel
fixSteps.instruction: Empty freezer and remove inner panel to access evaporator.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect and swap in the new thermistor.

whenToCallPro: If frost damage is extensive or evaporator appears leaking.

faq.a: Not reliably until the sensor is replaced.

title: Defrost Heater Fault
shortDescription: The defrost heater circuit is open or not functioning.
fullDescription:
E3 indicates the control did not see proper current draw from the defrost heater during a defrost cycle. The heater may be burned out, or the bi-metal thermostat in series with it may be open.

Frost will build up on the evaporator and cooling efficiency will drop until this is fixed.

fixSteps.title: Access evaporator
fixSteps.instruction: Remove rear freezer panel after emptying contents.

fixSteps.title: Test heater
fixSteps.instruction: Measure heater resistance; should show continuity around 25-35 ohms.

fixSteps.title: Replace failed part
fixSteps.instruction: Swap defrost heater or bimetal thermostat as needed.

whenToCallPro: If you are uncomfortable removing the evaporator cover or working around refrigerant lines.
videoSearchQuery: Maytag freezer E3 defrost heater replace

faq.a: Short-term only; frost will quickly stop cooling.

title: Evaporator Fan Motor Fault
shortDescription: The evaporator fan is not spinning at commanded speed.
fullDescription:
E4 indicates the evaporator fan motor is not reporting the expected RPM feedback. Without airflow across the coil, the freezer cannot cool uniformly.

Check for ice blocking the fan blade before replacing the motor.

fixSteps.title: Manual defrost
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug and allow any ice near the fan to melt.

fixSteps.title: Test motor
fixSteps.instruction: If fan still doesn't run, check voltage at the motor connector.

whenToCallPro: If freezer needs to be moved or refrigerant access is required.
videoSearchQuery: Maytag freezer E4 evaporator fan motor

faq.q: Why is there ice around the fan?
faq.a: Usually a failed defrost component allowing frost to accumulate.

title: Condenser Fan Fault
shortDescription: The condenser fan on the back of the freezer is not running.
fullDescription:
E5 indicates the condenser fan, which cools the compressor and condenser coil, has stopped working. The compressor may overheat and shut down on its overload protector.

Check for blade obstructions and debris before replacing the motor.

causes.cause: Debris or pet hair in condenser

fixSteps.title: Pull freezer out
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug and carefully pull the freezer away from the wall.

fixSteps.title: Clean coils and fan
fixSteps.instruction: Vacuum dust and debris from the condenser and fan blade.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor if needed
fixSteps.instruction: If fan still won't run, replace the condenser fan motor.

whenToCallPro: If the compressor is making unusual noises alongside the fan issue.
videoSearchQuery: Maytag freezer E5 condenser fan motor

faq.q: How often should I clean the coils?
faq.a: Every 6-12 months, more often with pets.

title: Freezer Temperature Too High
shortDescription: The freezer has warmed above the safe food storage threshold.
fullDescription:
FE is a high-temperature warning indicating the freezer compartment is above approximately 15F for an extended period. Causes range from a door left open to a sealed-system problem.

Check obvious issues first (door, load, vents) before assuming a major failure.

fixSteps.title: Close and seal door
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure door is fully closed and gasket seals evenly.

fixSteps.title: Clear vents
fixSteps.instruction: Rearrange contents so rear and side vents are not blocked.

fixSteps.title: Monitor temperature
fixSteps.instruction: Allow up to 24 hours for freezer to return to normal.

whenToCallPro: If temperature does not recover within 24 hours, sealed-system service is needed.
videoSearchQuery: Maytag freezer FE high temperature warning

faq.a: Often just a door issue; otherwise it can indicate compressor or refrigerant problems.

title: Door Open Alert
shortDescription: The freezer door has been open too long.
fullDescription:
OP is displayed when the door switch has detected an open door beyond the alarm delay, typically 3 to 5 minutes. It is an informational alert.

Close the door to dismiss. If OP persists with the door closed, the door switch itself may be faulty.

fixSteps.title: Close door fully
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure no items are blocking the door.

fixSteps.title: Test door switch
fixSteps.instruction: If code persists, check switch continuity when pressed.

fixSteps.title: Replace switch
fixSteps.instruction: Install new door switch if faulty.

whenToCallPro: Rarely needed unless door hinge is damaged.
videoSearchQuery: Maytag freezer OP door open code

faq.a: Check the door switch or alignment.

title: Control Lock Active
shortDescription: Control panel lock has been activated.
fullDescription:
CL indicates the keypad has been locked to prevent accidental changes. Press and hold the lock button for 3 seconds to unlock.

No fault has occurred.

causes.cause: Lock button pressed intentionally or accidentally

fixSteps.title: Unlock panel
fixSteps.instruction: Press and hold the lock or designated button for 3 seconds.

videoSearchQuery: Maytag freezer CL control lock unlock

faq.q: How do I prevent accidental lock?
faq.a: Keep young children from pressing the panel.

title: Display Test or Stuck Segments
shortDescription: All display segments lit during self-test, or display board fault.
fullDescription:
The 88 (or FF) indicator appears briefly at power-on as a display self-test. If it remains lit, the display board or control board ribbon cable may be faulty.

Power cycle first; if persistent, service is needed.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug freezer for 5 minutes, then restore power.

fixSteps.title: Check ribbon cable
fixSteps.instruction: If still stuck, reseat the display ribbon cable.

fixSteps.title: Replace display
fixSteps.instruction: Install new display board if problem persists.

whenToCallPro: If the control board itself is suspected.

faq.a: At boot, yes. If it stays, the display has failed.
